chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

I asked him about a man whose garment is affected by something that renders it najis, then he forgets to wash it and performs salat in it, then later remembers that he had not washed it. Should he repeat the salat? He said: He does not repeat it; the salat has passed and it has been recorded for him.

So it does not contradict the distinction that we mentioned, because the correct way regarding this report is that we interpret it as referring to when the time of the salat has already passed. For whenever one forgets to wash the najasah from the garment, repeating it is only required of him so long as he remains within the time; but when the time has passed, then there is no repetition upon him. And that has already been mentioned in the narration of Abī Baṣīr. And that which indicates the distinction we mentioned is what follows.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the obligatory prayer that was performed
key_terms.الْوَقْتِ: the legally appointed time of the salat
key_terms.ثَوْبَهُ: his garment or clothing in which salat was performed
key_terms.يَغْسِلَهُ: to wash it, meaning removing the impurity
key_terms.يَنْسَى: he forgets, indicating inadvertence rather than deliberate neglect

ai.seo_question: Does a person repeat salat if he forgot that his garment had najasah on it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of praying in a garment affected by najasah when one forgot to wash it. The narration states that if he remembers after the salat, he does not repeat it, and the compiler explains this as applying to the case where the time of the salat has already passed.
